html:
The Lost Boys of Sudan were some 20,000 boys, mostly Dinka and Nuer, who fled the Second Sudanese Civil War in the late 1980s. They walked hundreds of kilometres to refugee camps in Ethiopia and later Kenya.

The war pitted the government in Khartoum against rebels in the south. From around 1987 government forces and militias attacked villages in southern Sudan. Many boys who were out herding cattle escaped while their families were killed or scattered. They trekked in large groups, through hunger, thirst, wild animals and attacks, to camps across the Ethiopian border. Many died on the way.

In 1991 the government of Ethiopia fell and the boys were driven out. They walked back through Sudan and in 1992 reached the Kakuma refugee camp in northern Kenya, where many grew up.

In 2001 about 3,800 of them were resettled in the United States, and aid workers' name for them, taken from Peter Pan, became widely known. Some later returned to help build South Sudan, independent from 2011.
sum: The Lost Boys of Sudan were some 20,000 boys, mostly Dinka and Nuer, who fled the Second Sudanese Civil War in the late 1980s. They walked hundreds of kilometres to refugee camps in Ethiopia and later Kenya.
